## Summary
- Add `redaction.custom_secrets` so teams can define inline custom secret regexes in settings with per-key local overrides.
- Add `.entire/redactors/` rule packs with YAML/JSON parsing, sample validation, recursive discovery, and `.entire/redactors/local/` support for personal rules.
- Document the configuration surfaces, distribution guidance, troubleshooting, and security/privacy considerations.

## Why
Teams have internal credential shapes and custom token prefixes that the built-in redactors cannot know about. This gives them a repo-local way to ship redaction rules without waiting for a core CLI release or a hosted marketplace.

## Validation
- `mise run check`
- `mise run lint`

## Notes
- Rule sample mismatches and invalid regexes warn but do not fail configuration loading, so one bad custom rule does not disable the rest of redaction.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches the core redaction pipeline and startup configuration, so bugs could cause under-redaction (secret leakage) or over-redaction in transcripts; changes are mitigated by warn-and-skip behavior and extensive tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds user-defined secret redaction on top of existing detectors via two new configuration surfaces: inline `redaction.custom_secrets` in settings (with per-key merge/override between `settings.json` and `settings.local.json`) and YAML/JSON rule packs auto-discovered under `.entire/redactors/` (recursive, with optional `samples[]` self-tests that warn on mismatch).
> 
> Wires these rules into redaction initialization (`EnsureRedactionConfigured`) and into `redact.String()` as an additional “secret” layer, updates `entire enable` to ignore `.entire/redactors/local/` via `.entire/.gitignore`, and adds docs plus comprehensive tests for settings merge, pack parsing/loading, sample validation, and logging behavior.

@@ -78,6 +78,128 @@ All detected secrets are replaced with `REDACTED`. PII matches are replaced with
 
 To reduce over-redaction, Entire preserves structural transcript fields such as IDs and paths, leaves placeholder values alone, and redacts only credential values for bounded key/value forms. Placeholders are detected by exact match (e.g. `changeme`, `example`, `placeholder`, `your_password`, `your_secret`, prior `REDACTED`/`[REDACTED]`/`<REDACTED>` markers) or by shape: shell expansions like `${DB_PASSWORD}`, bracketed names like `<password>` or `<your-db-password>`, and mask runs of three or more `*`/`x`/`.`/`-` (so `***`, `xxxx`, `....`, `----` all match). When a connection string contains a real password, it is redacted as a unit because partial fragments can still expose sensitive material; connection strings whose passwords are placeholders are left intact.
 
+## Customizing redaction
+
+The built-in detectors handle well-known secret formats. For anything else you don't want stored in transcripts — internal credential shapes the bundled scanners don't know about, project codenames, or specific words and phrases you'd rather keep out of session archives — Entire offers two extension surfaces. Both run plain regex matching against transcript content, so the rules can target any string pattern, not just credentials. Both feed the same engine and run as their own layer between connection-string detection and bounded credential KV detection.
+
+### Surface 1: Inline `redaction.custom_redactions`
+
+Add a label → regex map under `redaction.custom_redactions` in `.entire/settings.json`:
+
+```json
+{
+  "redaction": {
+    "custom_redactions": {
+      "acme_token":  "ACME_TOKEN_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}",
+      "internal_id": "INTERNAL_[a-z]{6}_[0-9]{4}"
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+- The label is for diagnostics only; matches are replaced with the bare `REDACTED` token (matching the built-in secret layers, not the `[REDACTED_<LABEL>]` token used for PII).
+- Regexes follow [Go's RE2 syntax](https://pkg.go.dev/regexp/syntax). No lookarounds, no backreferences.
+- A failed compile is logged once at startup and the rule is skipped — it will never crash the redactor.
+- Override in `.entire/settings.local.json` for personal additions; entries merge per-key (override replaces the same key, leaves other keys intact).
+
+### Surface 2: Rule packs
+
+Drop a YAML or JSON file into `.entire/redactors/`:
+
+```yaml
+# .entire/redactors/acme-internal.yaml
+name: acme-internal              # MUST match the filename stem
+version: 1.0.0
+description: Internal ACME service tokens
+rules:
+  - id: acme-token
+    description: Long-lived ACME service tokens
+    regex: 'ACME_TOKEN_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}'
+    samples:
+      - { input: "REDACTED", redacted: true  }
+      - { input: "ACME_TOKEN_short",                     redacted: false }
+  - id: acme-session
+    regex: 'asess_[a-f0-9]{32}'
+```
+
+Equivalent JSON form:
+
+```json
+{
+  "name": "acme-internal",
+  "version": "1.0.0",
+  "rules": [
+    {
+      "id": "acme-token",
+      "regex": "ACME_TOKEN_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}",
+      "samples": [
+        { "input": "REDACTED", "redacted": true  },
+        { "input": "ACME_TOKEN_short",                     "redacted": false }
+      ]
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+**Required fields:** `name` (must equal the filename stem — `acme-internal.yaml` → `acme-internal`), `version` (any string; semver recommended), and `rules[]` (at least one entry, each with `id` and `regex`).
+
+**Optional fields:** `description` (pack-level and rule-level), and `rules[].samples[]` (see "Self-tests" below).
+
+A pack does not have to target credentials. The same shape works for any string pattern you don't want stored in transcripts — for example, a project codename or a small word list:
+
+```yaml
+# .entire/redactors/local/private-words.yaml
+name: private-words
+version: 1.0.0
+description: Project codenames and personal words to keep out of transcripts
+rules:
+  - id: codename-falcon
+    description: Internal project codename
+    regex: '(?i)\bproject[- ]?falcon\b'
+    samples:
+      - { input: "rolling out Project Falcon next week", redacted: true  }
+      - { input: "the falcon flew over",                  redacted: false }
+  - id: personal-words
+    description: Words I'd rather not see archived
+    regex: '(?i)\b(word_one|word_two)\b'
+```
+
+Putting personal lists under `.entire/redactors/local/` keeps them out of team commits (see "Distribution" below).
+
+### Self-tests via `samples[]`
+
+Each rule may declare an array of `{input, redacted}` pairs. On the next process startup after editing the pack, Entire runs each sample and emits a `slog.Warn` for any mismatch:
+
+```
+WARN  redactor pack sample mismatch  pack=.entire/redactors/acme-internal.yaml
+      rule=acme-token sample_index=0 sample_length=42 expected=true got=false
+```
+
+A failing sample never disables the rule — sample validation is informational. Use it to catch typos and false positives before they ship.
+
+### Distribution
+
+- **Within a team:** commit `.entire/settings.json` and/or `.entire/redactors/*` to your repo. Teammates pull and the rules apply.
+- **Across teams:** copy the pack file or share a link to a gist; recipients drop the file into their `.entire/redactors/`.
+- **Personal-only:** put the file in `.entire/redactors/local/` — `entire enable` writes that path into `.entire/.gitignore` so personal rules don't pollute team commits.
+
+### When to write a rule vs. file an issue
+
+Write a rule for:
+
+- Internal service tokens (`ACME_*`, `INTERNAL_*`) and custom env-var prefixes the bundled detectors don't know about.
+- Project-specific session formats.
+- Project codenames or other identifiers you don't want stored in transcripts.
+- Specific words or phrases you'd rather keep out of session archives.
+
+File an issue when the rule would benefit every Entire user (e.g., a major SaaS issued a new token format), when a built-in is producing false positives on common idioms in your codebase, or when a built-in is *not* catching a well-known shared format (we'd rather fix the built-in than have everyone ship the same custom rule).
+
+### Troubleshooting
+
+- **My rule doesn't redact anything.** Warnings about invalid patterns or sample mismatches appear on stderr when Entire initializes redaction, such as hooks that write checkpoints or `entire doctor`. Look for lines mentioning your label or pack path.
+- **My pack file is silently ignored.** Filenames must end in `.yaml`, `.yml`, or `.json`. Other extensions are skipped.
+- **I want to disable a rule temporarily.** Comment it out (prefix the YAML key with `#`) or remove the entry from `custom_redactions`. The rule reloads on the next CLI invocation.
+
 ## Limitations
 
 - **Best-effort.** Novel or low-entropy secrets (short passwords, predictable tokens) may not be caught.

+package redact
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"log/slog"
+	"strings"
+	"sync"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+// resetCustomRulesForTest clears the package-level config so tests don't leak
+// state into each other. Tests cannot run in parallel against the global, so
+// the helper is invoked at top-of-test in a t.Cleanup pattern.
+func resetCustomRulesForTest(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Helper()
+	customConfigMu.Lock()
+	customConfig = nil
+	customConfigMu.Unlock()
+	t.Cleanup(func() {
+		customConfigMu.Lock()
+		customConfig = nil
+		customConfigMu.Unlock()
+	})
+}
+
+// captureSlogForTest installs a slog handler that writes JSON lines to buf.
+// Returns a restore function the caller defers. Tests use this to assert
+// that ConfigureCustomRules emits the right warnings for failing samples.
+func captureSlogForTest(buf *bytes.Buffer) func() {
+	prev := slog.Default()
+	h := slog.NewJSONHandler(buf, &slog.HandlerOptions{Level: slog.LevelWarn})
+	slog.SetDefault(slog.New(h))
+	return func() { slog.SetDefault(prev) }
+}
+
+func TestConfigureCustomRules_SkipsInvalidRegexAndContinues(t *testing.T) {
+	resetCustomRulesForTest(t)
+
+	ConfigureCustomRules(CustomRulesConfig{
+		Inline: map[string]string{
+			"valid":   `[A-Z]{8}`,
+			"invalid": `[unterminated`,
+		},
+	})
+
+	cfg := getCustomRulesConfig()
+	if cfg == nil {
+		t.Fatal("expected config")
+	}
+	if got := len(cfg.rules); got != 1 {
+		t.Fatalf("rules: want 1 (invalid dropped), have %d", got)
+	}
+	if cfg.rules[0].label != "valid" {
+		t.Errorf("label: want valid, have %q", cfg.rules[0].label)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestConfigureCustomRules_ConcurrentReadsAndWrites(t *testing.T) {
+	resetCustomRulesForTest(t)
+
+	var wg sync.WaitGroup
+	wg.Add(2)
+	go func() {
+		defer wg.Done()
+		for range 100 {
+			ConfigureCustomRules(CustomRulesConfig{Inline: map[string]string{"x": `[a-z]+`}})
+		}
+	}()
+	go func() {
+		defer wg.Done()
+		for range 100 {
+			_ = getCustomRulesConfig()
+		}
+	}()
+	wg.Wait()
+}
+
+func TestString_CustomRuleEndToEnd(t *testing.T) {
+	resetCustomRulesForTest(t)
+	ConfigureCustomRules(CustomRulesConfig{
+		Inline: map[string]string{
+			"acme_token": `ACME_TOKEN_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}`,
+		},
+	})
+
+	in := "REDACTED REDACTED"
+	out := String(in)
+
+	if got := strings.Count(out, "REDACTED"); got != 2 {
+		t.Errorf("REDACTED count: want 2, have %d in %q", got, out)
+	}
+	if contains(t, out, "ACME_TOKEN_") {
+		t.Errorf("raw token leaked into output: %q", out)
+	}
+	if contains(t, out, "[REDACTED_") {
+		t.Errorf("custom rule used PII-style token: %q", out)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestString_CustomRuleNotConfiguredIsNoop(t *testing.T) {
+	resetCustomRulesForTest(t)
+
+	in := "T_aaaaaa T_bbbbbb"
+	if got := String(in); got != in {
+		t.Errorf("expected unchanged %q, got %q", in, got)
+	}
+}
+
+func contains(t *testing.T, s, sub string) bool {
+	t.Helper()
+	return strings.Contains(s, sub)
+}
+
+func TestConfigureCustomRules_SamplesPassEmitNoWarn(t *testing.T) {
+	resetCustomRulesForTest(t)
+
+	var buf bytes.Buffer
+	restore := captureSlogForTest(&buf)
+	defer restore()
+
+	pack := &Pack{
+		Name:    "ok",
+		Version: "1.0.0",
+		Rules: []Rule{
+			{
+				ID:    "match",
+				Regex: `T_[a-z]{6}`,
+				Samples: []Sample{
+					{Input: "T_abcdef", Redacted: true},
+					{Input: "T_short", Redacted: false},
+				},
+			},
+		},
+		sourcePath: "ok.yaml",
+	}
+
+	ConfigureCustomRules(CustomRulesConfig{Packs: []*Pack{pack}})
+
+	if strings.Contains(buf.String(), `"sample"`) {
+		t.Errorf("expected no sample warnings, got logs: %s", buf.String())
+	}
+}
+
+func TestConfigureCustomRules_SamplesFailEmitWarnButKeepRule(t *testing.T) {
+	resetCustomRulesForTest(t)
+
+	var buf bytes.Buffer
+	restore := captureSlogForTest(&buf)
+	defer restore()
+
+	pack := &Pack{
+		Name:    "bad-sample",
+		Version: "1.0.0",
+		Rules: []Rule{
+			{
+				ID:    "match",
+				Regex: `T_[a-z]{6}`,
+				Samples: []Sample{
+					{Input: "no_match", Redacted: true},
+				},
+			},
+		},
+		sourcePath: "bad-sample.yaml",
+	}
+
+	ConfigureCustomRules(CustomRulesConfig{Packs: []*Pack{pack}})
+
+	logs := buf.String()
+	if !strings.Contains(logs, `bad-sample.yaml`) {
+		t.Errorf("warn missing pack path: %s", logs)
+	}
+	if !strings.Contains(logs, `"rule":"match"`) {
+		t.Errorf("warn missing rule id: %s", logs)
+	}
+
+	cfg := getCustomRulesConfig()
+	if cfg == nil || len(cfg.rules) != 1 {
+		t.Fatalf("rule should remain active despite failing sample, have %v", cfg)
+	}
+}
+
+func REDACTED(t *testing.T) {
+	resetCustomRulesForTest(t)
+
+	var buf bytes.Buffer
+	restore := captureSlogForTest(&buf)
+	defer restore()
+
+	const sample = "REDACTED"
+	pack := &Pack{
+		Name:    "safe-logs",
+		Version: "1.0.0",
+		Rules: []Rule{
+			{
+				ID:      "sample",
+				Regex:   `NEVER_MATCHES`,
+				Samples: []Sample{{Input: sample, Redacted: true}},
+			},
+		},
+		sourcePath: "safe-logs.yaml",
+	}
+
+	ConfigureCustomRules(CustomRulesConfig{Packs: []*Pack{pack}})
+
+	logs := buf.String()
+	if strings.Contains(logs, sample) {
+		t.Fatalf("sample mismatch log leaked raw sample: %s", logs)
+	}
+	if !strings.Contains(logs, `"sample_index":0`) {
+		t.Errorf("warn missing sample index: %s", logs)
+	}
+	if !strings.Contains(logs, `"sample_length":`) {
+		t.Errorf("warn missing sample length: %s", logs)
+	}
+}

+package redact
+
+import (
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+func TestParsePack_Valid(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	tests := []struct {
+		name        string
+		sourcePath  string
+		body        string
+		wantRules   int
+		wantSamples int
+	}{
+		{
+			name:       "yaml",
+			sourcePath: "acme-internal.yaml",
+			body: `
+name: acme-internal
+version: 1.0.0
+description: Internal ACME tokens
+rules:
+  - id: acme-token
+    regex: 'ACME_TOKEN_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}'
+    samples:
+      - { input: "REDACTED", redacted: true }
+      - { input: "ACME_TOKEN_short", redacted: false }
+  - id: acme-session
+    regex: 'asess_[a-f0-9]{32}'
+`,
+			wantRules:   2,
+			wantSamples: 2,
+		},
+		{
+			name:       "json",
+			sourcePath: "acme-internal.json",
+			body: `{
+  "name": "acme-internal",
+  "version": "1.0.0",
+  "rules": [
+    {
+      "id": "acme-token",
+      "regex": "ACME_TOKEN_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}"
+    }
+  ]
+}`,
+			wantRules: 1,
+		},
+	}
+
+	for _, tc := range tests {
+		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			t.Parallel()
+
+			pack, err := ParsePack([]byte(tc.body), tc.sourcePath)
+			if err != nil {
+				t.Fatalf("ParsePack: %v", err)
+			}
+			if pack.Name != "acme-internal" {
+				t.Errorf("Name: want acme-internal, have %q", pack.Name)
+			}
+			if pack.Version != "1.0.0" {
+				t.Errorf("Version: want 1.0.0, have %q", pack.Version)
+			}
+			if len(pack.Rules) != tc.wantRules {
+				t.Fatalf("Rules: want %d, have %d", tc.wantRules, len(pack.Rules))
+			}
+			if pack.Rules[0].ID != "acme-token" {
+				t.Errorf("Rules[0].ID: want acme-token, have %q", pack.Rules[0].ID)
+			}
+			if len(pack.Rules[0].Samples) != tc.wantSamples {
+				t.Errorf("Rules[0].Samples: want %d, have %d", tc.wantSamples, len(pack.Rules[0].Samples))
+			}
+		})
+	}

content.text:
Looking over PR #1076 "Add user-defined redaction rules and rule packs" (currently REVIEW_REQUIRED, all CI green).

## Verdict

Looks good to ship. Architecture is clean, error paths are warn-and-skip (right call for a security feature — one bad rule shouldn't silence the rest), and test coverage is thorough. A few comments below — none are blockers.

## Strengths

- **Two surfaces, one engine.** Inline `custom_redactions` and pack files feed the same compiled-rule list; the layered split in `redact.String()` is a one-liner add (layer 5) — minimal risk to existing detectors.
- **Warn-and-skip across the board.** Invalid regex, missing dir, unreadable file, symlink, schema error, sample mismatch — none are fatal. The settings-load and pack-walk paths cannot kill redaction.
- **Strict schema parsing.** `DisallowUnknownFields` on JSON, `KnownFields(true)` on YAML, *and* an extra `Decode(&extra)` to reject trailing content / multi-doc YAML. Good belt-and-suspenders.
- **Per-key local override semantics** (`mergeRedaction`) are correct and tested at the merge layer (`TestLoadMerged_CustomRedactionsPerKeyOverride`).
- **`redactors/local/`** convention + `.entire/.gitignore` integration is a nice UX touch for personal rules.
- **Privacy-aware logging.** `REDACTED` is a great regression guard — sample inputs are summarized by `sample_index` + `sample_length`, never raw.

## Things worth a second look

1. **`paths.AbsPath` failure fallback walks CWD** — `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:380-386`. If `WorktreeRoot` fails (e.g., process started outside a repo, but settings somehow loaded), `packsDir` falls back to the relative `.entire/redactors`. `LoadPacks` then walks that path relative to CWD, which can pick up an unrelated `.entire/redactors/` if someone happened to be in a directory that has one. Low likelihood, but the safer move is to skip pack-loading entirely on `paths.AbsPath` failure. Optional.

2. **No guard against over-broad regex (e.g. `.*`, `(.+)`).** A user-supplied `.*` would redact every transcript. Sample-validation catches this only if they wrote samples. Consider either (a) a doc warning under "Customizing redaction" that an unanchored permissive regex will eat everything, or (b) rejecting patterns that match the empty string at compile time. Doc fix is enough IMO.

3. **No de-duplication across packs.** `validatePack` rejects duplicate rule IDs *within* a pack, but two packs can both define `id: api-key`. Behavior is correct (both run, both labels stay distinct via `pack.Name+"."+rule.ID`), but if two packs happen to have the same `name` (e.g., one in root + one in `local/`), the labels collide in logs. Worth a one-liner check in `LoadPacks` to warn on duplicate pack names, or just document it.

4. **Filename-stem-must-match-pack-name** is enforced (`packs.go:107`). Justification is good (consistent logs/discovery), but it's a UX papercut on rename and isn't documented in `docs/security-and-privacy.md`. Add one line to the "Required fields" section: "`name` must equal the filename stem (e.g., `acme-internal.yaml` → `acme-internal`)" — actually you already have this. Nevermind, good.

5. **Per-call linear scan.** `detectCustomRules` runs `FindAllStringIndex` per rule per `String()` call. Fine for tens of rules; with hundreds of pack rules and high-frequency transcript scanning, worth keeping in mind. Not a today-problem.

6. **Minor test gap:** symlinked *subdirectory* (vs. symlinked file) isn't covered. `WalkDir` won't follow them by default, and `d.Type()&fs.ModeSymlink` will skip them, but a one-line test would lock the behavior in.

7. **`Pack.Description` / `Rule.Description`** are accepted by the schema but never surfaced anywhere (no logs, no `entire doctor`). Fine to keep as human-readability fields, but a comment to that effect on the struct would prevent "why isn't this shown?" issues later.

## Nits

- `EnsureRedactionConfigured` is wrapped in `sync.Once`, which means rule edits require a process restart. That's the right model, but it's not in the docs — worth one line under "Troubleshooting" ("rule changes take effect on the next CLI invocation"). You already have something close ("The rule reloads on the next CLI invocation") under "disable a rule temporarily" — maybe make it general.
- `redact/custom.go:25` — `label` on `compiledCustomRule` is never read at redact time (regions are emitted with empty label). Comment already says this; could simplify by dropping the field entirely and only keeping it in log-emission scope. Cosmetic.

Happy to push fixes for any of these if you want — say the word.

201	- **I want to disable a rule temporarily.** Comment it out (prefix the YAML key with `#`) or remove the entry from `custom_redactions`. The rule reloads on the next CLI invocation.
202	
203	## Limitations
204	
205	- **Best-effort.** Novel or low-entropy secrets (short passwords, predictable tokens) may not be caught.
206	- **Filenames and binary data.** Secrets in filenames, binary files, or deeply nested structures may not be detected.
207	- **JSONL skip rules.** Entire skips scanning fields named `signature`, fields ending in `id`/`ids`, structural-path fields (`filepath`, `file_path`, `cwd`, `root`, `directory`, `dir`, `path`), and objects whose `type` starts with `image` or equals `base64` — all to avoid false positives.
208	- **Custom PII patterns are user-authored.** Teams own the correctness of their `custom_patterns`. An invalid regex is logged and skipped, not enforced.
209	- **Users are ultimately responsible** for reviewing what they commit and push. Redaction is a safety net, not a guarantee.
210	
211	## Telemetry
212	
213	The CLI captures anonymous usage analytics by default. Sent to PostHog with `DisableGeoIP` enabled. Captured per command: command name, selected agent, whether Entire is enabled in the repo, CLI version, OS/arch, and **names** of flags passed (never their values). The distinct ID is a hashed machine identifier (`machineid.ProtectedID`), not a user identity.

79	To reduce over-redaction, Entire preserves structural transcript fields such as IDs and paths, leaves placeholder values alone, and redacts only credential values for bounded key/value forms. Placeholders are detected by exact match (e.g. `changeme`, `example`, `placeholder`, `your_password`, `your_secret`, prior `REDACTED`/`[REDACTED]`/`<REDACTED>` markers) or by shape: shell expansions like `${DB_PASSWORD}`, bracketed names like `<password>` or `<your-db-password>`, and mask runs of three or more `*`/`x`/`.`/`-` (so `***`, `xxxx`, `....`, `----` all match). When a connection string contains a real password, it is redacted as a unit because partial fragments can still expose sensitive material; connection strings whose passwords are placeholders are left intact.
80	
81	## Customizing redaction
82	
83	The built-in detectors handle well-known secret formats. For anything else you don't want stored in transcripts — internal credential shapes the bundled scanners don't know about, project codenames, or specific words and phrases you'd rather keep out of session archives — Entire offers two extension surfaces. Both run plain regex matching against transcript content, so the rules can target any string pattern, not just credentials. Both feed the same engine and run as their own layer between connection-string detection and bounded credential KV detection.

### Troubleshooting

- **My rule doesn't redact anything.** Warnings about invalid patterns or sample mismatches appear on stderr when Entire initializes redaction, such as hooks that write checkpoints or `entire doctor`. Look for lines mentioning your label or pack path.
- **My pack file is silently ignored.** Filenames must end in `.yaml`, `.yml`, or `.json`. Other extensions are skipped.
- **My rule edits aren't taking effect.** Redaction settings are read once per CLI invocation. Adding, editing, removing, or commenting out (`#` prefix in YAML) a rule applies on the next `entire` command — there is no hot-reload inside a long-running session.

1	package redact
2	
3	import (
4		"log/slog"
5		"regexp"
6		"sync"
7	)
8	
9	// CustomRulesConfig configures inline custom_redactions and parsed rule packs.
10	type CustomRulesConfig struct {
11		// Inline maps a label (used only in logs/diagnostics) to a Go RE2 regex
12		// string. Failed compilations are logged via slog.Warn and dropped.
13		Inline map[string]string
14	
15		// Packs are pre-parsed rule packs (see LoadPacks). Per-rule regex
16		// compilation failures are logged and dropped; sample mismatches are
17		// logged but do not drop the rule.
18		Packs []*Pack
19	}
20	
21	// customRulesState holds the compiled regexes used by detectCustomRules.
22	// Labels are not retained: detectCustomRules emits regions with an empty
23	// label so that matches are replaced with the bare REDACTED token used by
24	// the other secret layers. Labels are only meaningful during configuration,
25	// where they appear in slog warnings for compile failures and sample
26	// mismatches; once those have been logged the label is no longer needed.
27	type customRulesState struct {
28		rules []*regexp.Regexp
29	}
30	
31	var (
32		customConfig   *customRulesState
33		customConfigMu sync.RWMutex
34	)
35	
36	// ConfigureCustomRules compiles user-defined redaction rules and stores the
37	// result for use by redact.String(). Sample-validation runs here too, so
38	// failures surface the next time any process initializes redaction.
39	//
40	// Call once at process startup after loading settings. Thread-safe.
41	func ConfigureCustomRules(cfg CustomRulesConfig) {
42		state := &customRulesState{}
43	
44		for label, pattern := range cfg.Inline {
45			compiled, ok := compileCustomRule(
46				label,
47				pattern,
48				"skipping invalid custom_redactions pattern",
49				slog.String("label", label),
50			)
51			if ok {
52				state.rules = append(state.rules, compiled)
53			}
54		}
55	
56		for _, pack := range cfg.Packs {
57			for _, rule := range pack.Rules {
58				compiled, ok := compileCustomRule(
59					pack.Name+"."+rule.ID,
60					rule.Regex,
61					"skipping invalid pack rule",
62					slog.String("pack", pack.sourcePath),
63					slog.String("rule", rule.ID),
64				)
65				if ok {
66					state.rules = append(state.rules, compiled)
67					runRuleSamples(pack, rule, compiled.regex)
68				}
69			}
70		}
71	
72		customConfigMu.Lock()
73		defer customConfigMu.Unlock()
74		customConfig = state
75	}
76	
77	func compileCustomRule(label, pattern, warning string, attrs ...any) (compiledCustomRule, bool) {
78		compiled, err := regexp.Compile(pattern)
79		if err != nil {
80			attrs = append(attrs, slog.String("error", err.Error()))
81			slog.Warn(warning, attrs...)
82			return compiledCustomRule{}, false
83		}
84		return compiledCustomRule{label: label, regex: compiled}, true
85	}
86	
87	// runRuleSamples checks each sample against the compiled regex and logs a
88	// warning per mismatch. Failures never drop the rule — sample validation
89	// is informational, not gating.
90	func runRuleSamples(pack *Pack, rule Rule, compiled *regexp.Regexp) {
91		for i, s := range rule.Samples {
92			got := compiled.MatchString(s.Input)
93			if got != s.Redacted {
94				slog.Warn("redactor pack sample mismatch",
95					slog.String("pack", pack.sourcePath),
96					slog.String("rule", rule.ID),
97					slog.Int("sample_index", i),
98					slog.Int("sample_length", len(s.Input)),
99					slog.Bool("expected", s.Redacted),
100					slog.Bool("got", got))
101			}
102		}
103	}
104	
105	// getCustomRulesConfig returns the currently-configured custom rules.
106	// Returns nil if ConfigureCustomRules has never been called.
107	func getCustomRulesConfig() *customRulesState {
108		customConfigMu.RLock()
109		defer customConfigMu.RUnlock()
110		return customConfig
111	}
112	
113	// detectCustomRules returns tagged regions for every match of every
114	// configured custom rule. Returns nil if no rules are configured.
115	//
116	// All regions use an empty label so they are replaced with the bare
117	// "REDACTED" token used by the built-in secret layers, not the
118	// "[REDACTED_<LABEL>]" token used by PII.
119	func detectCustomRules(cfg *customRulesState, s string) []taggedRegion {
120		if cfg == nil || len(cfg.rules) == 0 || s == "" {
121			return nil
122		}
123		var regions []taggedRegion
124		for _, rule := range cfg.rules {
125			for _, loc := range rule.regex.FindAllStringIndex(s, -1) {
126				regions = append(regions, taggedRegion{region: region{loc[0], loc[1]}})
127			}
128		}
129		return regions
130	}

3. `9abac3efe` — `test(redact): cover symlinked subdirs in LoadPacks` — locks in lstat-based skip behavior for symlinked subdirectories, complementing the existing symlinked-file test.
4. `63c98fc68` — `docs(redact): document regex risks and drop dead label field` — adds an "anchor your patterns" warning about `.*`/`.+`, generalizes the reload note (any change applies on next invocation), and removes `compiledCustomRule.label` since nothing read it.
